content:
Maya Patel: Hey team — our production is getting lots of 429s this morning. We did a controlled burst test (200 req/s) from a single IP and expected per-API-key throttles, but the responses say scope=organization. Can someone triage?

Jin Park: Sorry you're hitting this, Maya. Can you paste a sample curl and one full 429 response body (headers + body) and the X-Request-ID? Also which API key did you use and whether the test used a shared IP/proxy?

Maya Patel: nvm I grabbed one. curl we used: 
```
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-abc123" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -H "X-Forwarded-For: 54.210.12.34" \n  -d '{"model":"gpt-large","prompt":"hello","max_tokens":10}'
```
Response: 
```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "rate_limit_exceeded",
    "message": "Quota exceeded",
    "details": {
      "scope":"organization",
      "limit":{"unit":"minute","allowed":100000},
      "retry_after": 3
    },
    "request_id":"req_01H8ZK6X5A9"
  }
}
```
Header snippet: `x-rate-limit-scope: organization` and `x-request-id: req_01H8ZK6X5A9`

Maya Patel: We have two API keys under the same org but expected each key to have independent burst headroom. This is blocking our rollout tests.

rate-limit-bot: Alert: 429 spike detected on svc-api-us-east-1 — 17% of requests are returning rate_limit_exceeded (scope=organization). Investigating.

Jin Park: Thanks — I see the x-request-id. First pass: is your test sending the API key in every request? The curl you pasted does. Are you also routing via a pooling proxy that re-uses one IP for different customers? That could trigger IP-based buckets.

Maya Patel: No proxy, single host from our CI. We rotated keys and repeated; same behavior — scope=organization consistently.

Evan Gomez: Jumping in — I pulled the rate limiter logs for req_01H8ZK6X5A9. The decision path shows: mapQuotaScope -> matched scope: organization (org_id: org_9876), reason: ip_lookup_fallback.

Evan Gomez: quick excerpt (sanitized): 
```
[2024-10-12T09:13:22Z] req=req_01H8ZK6X5A9 src_ip=54.210.12.34 header_api_key=sk-prod-abc123 ctx_api_key_id=key_42 map_scope_flow=ip_first lookup(api_key)->found key_42 lookup(ip)->found shared_bucket(org_9876) decision=ORG_BUCKET
```

Jin Park: That log line is odd — flow says `ip_first` even though header_api_key is present. The intended mapping order should be: api_key -> key_bucket, then ip -> ip_bucket, then org fallback. Looks like the ip-based code path accidentally overrides an existing api_key bucket.

Maya Patel: Is this a config setting? We didn't change anything. We only increased traffic.

Evan Gomez: Not a config change on your side. Looking at recent deploys, there's a regression in the rate limiter (release v2.14.1). The bug is in rate_limiter.go: mapScope() — a refactor introduced an early `if ip != nil { return ipBucket }` before checking for API key in some code paths. For normal clients that send API key + X-Forwarded-For, that causes org-level grouping for our multi-key customers.

Jin Park: Repro steps: 1) Send requests with header Authorization: sk-prod-abc123 and X-Forwarded-For set to same IP used by other keys. 2) Observe x-rate-limit-scope: organization. 3) Compare to pre-v2.14.1 behavior where x-rate-limit-scope was api_key.

Maya Patel: That matches what we see. Any ETA on a fix? This is causing real user-facing errors.

Evan Gomez: I pushed a hotfix branch that reorders the checks and adds unit tests for combined api_key+ip cases. Patch: `fix(rate-limiter): prefer api_key bucket when Authorization header present` — PR #3287. Deploying canary to us-east-1 now (instance group 3).

Jin Park: For immediate mitigation, if you can avoid sending X-Forwarded-For in your test (or set it to true client ip per key) we can avoid the ip-first logic until patch lands. But I know you said you can't change CI easily.

rate-limit-bot: Deploy event: v2.14.2-canary to svc-api-us-east-1 (group 3) started by Evan.

Evan Gomez: Canary is up. I manually hit the same burst from one test key and watched logs: map_scope_flow now shows `api_key_first` and `decision=KEY_BUCKET`. Request ids: req_01H8ZK6X5A9 -> new req_01H8ZK6X7B2.

Maya Patel: Retested from CI (ran the same 200 req/s job) — I see far fewer 429s, and x-rate-limit-scope: api_key on the ones that do 429. Progressing to a full rollout?

Jin Park: We're going to roll v2.14.2 to all us-east nodes in 10m once canary looks stable. After rollout, please re-run your burst and send any failing request ids.

Priya Rao: Heads up on billing: since your app incurred throttling caused by our bug, we can offer a credit for the period affected. Maya, can you share a short window (UTC) when you were blocked so we can compute credits?

Maya Patel: Block window: 2024-10-12 08:55:00 to 2024-10-12 09:20:00 UTC (approx). We ran multiple tries in that window while debugging.

Evan Gomez: Full rollout done at 2024-10-12T09:16:30Z across us-east. Post-rollout verification looks green. Logs show decision=KEY_BUCKET for the later requests.

Jin Park: Closing loop: root cause = regression in rate_limiter mapScope ordering introduced in v2.14.1; symptomatic behavior = organization-scoped 429s when API key + IP present; fix = reorder checks and add unit/integration tests; deploy = v2.14.2.

Maya Patel: Thanks team — we re-ran our suite and saw normal per-key limits. Appreciate the quick fix and the offer for credit.

Priya Rao: I'll open a billing ticket and loop you in (Maya) with details and the proposed credit.

Jin Park: Follow-ups: 1) We added an alert rule to detect sudden shift of x-rate-limit-scope -> organization for customers with multiple api keys. 2) We'll add a console toggle to prioritize per-key scoping for enterprise orgs (feature request). 3) Postmortem doc tracked in #postmortems with link: https://redwood.docs/postmortems/2024-10-12-rate-limit-scope-regression (will file shortly).

Evan Gomez: Commit for fix: `commit abcdef1234567890` (rate_limiter.go: mapScope reorder + added tests). Rollback plan ready if we see regressions.

Maya Patel: Marking this resolved on our side. Thanks everyone. :party_parrot: (reaction from team :thumbsup:)
